Subject: Mutual Action Plan & Eval: cost modeling, tokens/$ and runtime assumptions (ACME POC)

Emily / Tom —

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan that pairs the evaluation milestones with the cost assumptions we used to size the POC. High level asks: please review the milestones and confirm the data access timeline (S3 creds) and the evaluation success criteria (latency, p95 < 350ms; relevance > 0.6 on your scoring rubric).

Key cost assumptions called out in the MAP: tokens per request (avg 1.2k), batching target (8 reqs per batch for typical traffic), and prefix caching eligible % (expected 30% for your product search flows). Those three knobs drive the modeled tokens/$ significantly; the attached CSV shows sensitivity runs at 20/30/40% cache hit and batch sizes 4/8/16.

Next steps I propose:
- ACME confirms data access + POC users by 11/06
- We ship a sandbox with eval harness and example prompts by 11/09
- Joint evaluation window 11/10–11/24 (two-week run)
- Final recommendation and quote 11/30

See the attached MAP_ACME_v1.xlsx for the gantt, responsibilities, and the token_modeling_excerpt.csv for the cost sensitivity table. If you want a quick call to walk the assumptions we can do 30m Thurs morning.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Emily Cho <e.cho@acme.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Mutual Action Plan & Eval: cost modeling, tokens/$ and runtime assumptions (ACME POC)

Emily / Tom / team —

Thanks — I attached a compact excerpt (redwood-eval-plan.md) and a short CSV with the rerun numbers. Highlights:
- Baseline: 900 tokens/request, model throughput priced at $0.0009 per generation-token (hosted tier), request tokens = input+output accounted.
- Caching: 40% prefix cache reduces total generation tokens by ~36% (accounting for cache misses and cold-start overhead).
- Batching: at batch=8 we achieve ~18% per-token cost reduction vs batch=1 on our dedicated inference profiles; batch=16 gives incremental improvement but increases p95 latency risk.

Estimated POC run (two-week window at expected traffic):
- Token consumption (no cache, batch=1): 24M gen-tokens -> ~$21.6k
- Token consumption (40% cache, batch=8): 15.4M gen-tokens -> ~$13.9k
- Sensitivity: cache hit +/-10pp shifts cost by ~2.8k over the run; batch size swings +/-1.2k.

Action items I’ll deliver:
- Full MAP spreadsheet updated with these numbers (shared to Drive)
- Short deck slide that explains tradeoffs (cache vs batch vs latency) for the 11/05 sync

Marcus — I’ll be on the call to present the numbers if scheduled. Monica, flag anything for CS runbooks (metrics to log: cache hit ratio, avg batch size, p95 latency).

Best,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
